title: A colleague's social media post showing a patient's wound

header.contentArea: Professionalism: confidentiality, social media and raising concerns

GMC Making and using visual and audio recordings of patients (2011; updated 18 Dec 2024)

brief.scenario: Last night your fellow core trainee, Dr Callum Rennie, posted a photo on his public Instagram account, which has about 2,000 followers. It shows a patient's dehisced laparotomy wound. A distinctive tattoo on the patient's flank and the edge of a hospital wristband are visible. The caption reads: "Night shift on Ward 7. Didn't see that coming #surgeonlife". You recognise the patient as Mr Quigley from your ward. Dr Rennie has just walked in.
brief.task: Talk to Dr Rennie about the post and agree what happens next. The examiner may ask you questions at the end.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: A confidentiality breach still happening now. Get it taken down, then make sure it's reported, while treating him fairly.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Agreeing it's fine to keep quiet once he deletes it.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Callum, have you got a minute somewhere private? It's about your Instagram post."

grid.label: Private, non-judgemental opening
grid.fail: Confronts him in front of others, or opens with an accusation.
grid.pass: Finds somewhere private, says what it's about, and lets him speak.
grid.high: Keeps a calm, factual tone that keeps him in the conversation, and acknowledges he probably didn't mean harm.

grid.label: Explaining why it's a breach
grid.fail: Accepts that no name means no breach.
grid.pass: The tattoo, wristband, ward in the caption and the post's timestamp together can identify him; no explicit consent, so it breaches confidentiality.
grid.high: Adds dignity: a wound photo for likes, not care; and once shared it can't be controlled, even from a "private" account.

grid.label: Stopping the harm now
grid.pass: Asks him to delete the post now, while together, and the photo from his personal phone.
grid.high: Checks for other copies (shares, stories, backups), and knows clinical photos need consent and trust equipment or systems.

grid.label: Reporting and escalation
grid.fail: Agrees to keep it between them once deleted.
grid.pass: Explains it must be reported: consultant or educational supervisor, and the trust's incident/information governance route, today.
grid.high: Knows the trust must decide within 72 hours whether to notify the Information Commissioner; GMC only if local action is inadequate or it continues.

grid.label: The patient's interests
grid.fail: Doesn't consider the patient at all.
grid.pass: Says the patient should be told honestly by the team, with an apology, as the trust decides.
grid.high: Explains why: he may already have seen it, and hearing it from the team protects trust in his care.

grid.label: Handling pushback and support
grid.fail: Gets drawn into argument, or is persuaded by "everyone does it".
grid.pass: Holds the line calmly and explains the duty to patients comes before loyalty.
grid.high: Encourages him to report it himself first, suggests his defence body and supervisor, and offers to go with him.

grid.label: Knowing the current guidance
grid.fail: Cannot name any guidance, or cites only the 2013 social media guidance.
grid.pass: GMC Using social media as a medical professional (2024) under Good medical practice: no identifiable information without explicit consent.
grid.high: Knows the 2013 guidance was withdrawn in January 2024, and that education needs consent under the GMC recordings guidance.

grid.label: Record and follow-up
grid.pass: Notes what he saw, when, and what was agreed; checks it has been reported.
grid.high: Keeps it factual and confidential, and follows up with the consultant rather than discussing it with other colleagues.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Callum, can we talk somewhere private? It's about your Instagram post. I'm sure you didn't mean any harm, but I'm worried about it.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Dr Rennie: "It's educational. My account's basically private."

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Each detail on its own might not identify him, but the tattoo, wristband, ward in the caption and the post's timestamp together could. It's also his dignity: a wound shared for likes, not for his care. And once it's out, it can be screenshotted and shared.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Please delete it now, and the photo. Has it been shared or saved anywhere else? If a wound needs photographing for teaching, we get consent and use the trust's system, not our phones.

failures.move: Accepting that no name means no breach.
failures.consequence: The sum of details (tattoo, wristband, ward in the caption, the post's timestamp) can identify him; GMC guidance says so explicitly.

failures.move: Letting him take it down later.
failures.consequence: Every hour it stays up, more people can see, save and share it.

failures.move: Agreeing to keep it quiet once deleted.
failures.consequence: The breach has already happened; the trust must assess it, possibly notify the Information Commissioner, and tell the patient.
He stops listening, and the post stays up longer.

recovery.line: No name, but the tattoo, wristband and ward together make him recognisable.

recovery.when: He asks you to keep quiet
recovery.line: I can't, but I'll support you, and it's better coming from you first.

knowledge.fact: Individual details may not identify a patient, but the sum of information can; don't disclose identifiable information on social media without explicit consent (paras 19–20).
Maintain confidentiality in all professional digital communications (para 88); follow the social media guidance (para 91).
The 2013 guidance Doctors' use of social media was withdrawn on 30 January 2024.
The data controller notifies the Information Commissioner of a personal data breach within 72 hours where feasible, unless it is unlikely to pose a risk.
Contact the GMC if local action is inadequate, the local body is part of the problem, or the risk is immediate and serious (para 16).

recall.think: An identifiable patient on public social media, still visible now.
recall.say: "It has to come down now, and it has to be reported."

recall.trap: "No name on it" is not anonymous.
recall.finish: Trust tells the patient; support your colleague; GMC only if local action fails.

media.description: Our own mock-up of a social media post: a wound photo with a visible tattoo and wristband edge, the ward in the caption and the post's timestamp; no real patient

partner.opening: Dr Rennie has just come into the mess with a coffee. Please begin.
partner.actorBrief: You are Dr Callum Rennie, a core surgical trainee, friendly and well liked, a little defensive. Your ARCP is next month. Opening line: "Morning! Rough night. Did you see the wound on Ward 7?" You posted the photo at 3 am after a stressful night; you meant it as "interesting teaching" and didn't think about the tattoo or wristband. Your account is public but you think of it as private. Push back in turn: (1) "There's no name on it. It's educational." (2) "Loads of surgeons post stuff like this." (3) After deleting it: "So we can forget it now?" (4) If told it must be reported: "If this goes further, my ARCP's finished." If the candidate is calm and supportive, agree to delete it in front of them and to tell the consultant yourself. If they shame you, get angry and say you'll delete it later. Hidden: a friend has already screenshotted it and shared it to a group chat; reveal only if asked whether it has been shared.

reveals.trigger: Asks whether it has been shared
reveals.finding: "A mate screenshotted it for our group chat. About 30 people."
"Honestly, last night was grim. I just wanted to post something."

reveals.trigger: Asks him to delete it now
reveals.finding: He deletes the post in front of the candidate, and the photo from his camera roll.

reveals.trigger: Suggests he tells the consultant himself

push.question: What guidance applies?
push.expect: GMC Using social media as a medical professional (in effect January 2024) under Good medical practice 2024; 2013 guidance withdrawn.

push.question: Who else needs to know?
push.expect: Consultant or educational supervisor and the trust's incident/information governance route today; the patient, via the team.

push.question: When would you contact the GMC?
push.expect: If local action is inadequate, the breach continues or repeats, or there is an immediate serious risk.

curveballs.prompt: "He'd be fine with it. I'll ask him now and get his consent."
curveballs.safeAnswer: Consent can't be obtained retrospectively to cure the breach; it still needs reporting, and any future images go through trust consent and systems.
Ask for copies to be deleted, and include this in the report so the trust can act.
Acknowledges the friendship, offers support, but the duty to the patient comes first.
